data.exact_reserve_text: In settling claims provisions the Syndicate gives consideration to the probability and magnitude of future experience being more adverse than assumed and exercises a degree of caution in setting reserves where there is considerable uncertainty. In general, the uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience in an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin necessary to provide the necessary confidence in the provisions adequacy is relatively at its highest. As claims develop, and the ultimate cost of claims becomes more certain, the relative level of margin maintained should decrease. However, due to the uncertainty inherent in the estimation process, the actual overall claim provision may not always be in surplus. In 2017 the surplus was GBP 38.5m.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2017 the syndicate's gross claims outstanding were GBP 180.1m. Analysis of the gross claims development table indicates a modest net favourable prior-year development of approximately GBP 5.3m (about 2.9% of opening reserves), i.e. a release. The release reflects favourable claims development on older underwriting years together with reinsurance recoveries; 2017 itself was heavily impacted by US catastrophe activity (Harvey/Irma/Maria, California wildfires and Mexico earthquakes) which mainly affected the 2017 year of account and was largely mitigated by the reinsurance programme.
raw_causal_phrases: The performance in 2017 has been impacted by the worst year for catastrophes in the US for over a decade with Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the wildfires in California and earthquakes in Mexico causing insured market losses of $135 billion the costliest year on record (source: Munich Re).
The impact of the catastrophe losses on Syndicate 1910 net of reinsurance recoveries added 18.16 percentage points to the combined ratio.

The 2016 Year of Account has performed creditably given that it was affected by Hurricane Matthew and fires in Alberta, the year is forecast to be better than plan when it closes in 12 months time with a return of stamp of 11.9%.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was not given as a single gross movement line. The prior-year movement was derived from the gross claims development table (triangle) by excluding the two most recent underwriting years (2016,2017) and comparing each older year's current estimate to its previous diagonal. This is a triangle-derived figure; no explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' line was available. Triangle parsing had some ragged rows in the PDF text extraction; values are taken as printed and rounded to one decimal where appropriate. No explicit gross prior-year movement figure was found in the notes or narrative.
